offence_severity: Death to life imprisonment for 30 years without remission
number_of_offences: Charged with multiple offences, conviction upheld for all
key_evidence_accepted: Medical evidence shows that the deceased was raped and killed. DNA profiling of the articles Q, R and S which are the vaginal slide, rectal slide and dried blood on the hair of the deceased showed Y (male) STR. Blood sample of 'S' matched with the articles found on Q, R and S. The Appellant miserably failed to prove an alibi. Importantly, there is lack of any explanation for the scratch injuries found on the body of the Appellant.
witness_credibility: PW-2 (father of victim) along with his family members attended a ceremony at the house of one 'AM' in the evening. His 11 years old daughter went missing and was found dead next morning. PW-4 deposed that he runs a small hotel in the village and the deceased visited his shop to purchase Kurkure at 9.00 p.m. 15 minutes thereafter, the Appellant visited the shop to purchase namkeen. PW-9 stated that the Appellant and 'S' visited his house on 15.04.2017. Their eyes were red, hair was scattered and they were scared. They informed him that they have committed a big scandal.
trial_duration: Offence: 14.04.2017; Trial judgment: 03.11.2017; High Court: 09.05.2018; Supreme Court: 2022
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Shri Singh, Amartya Kanjilal, Ms. Sayali Kadu, Ms. Adebba Mujahid; Counsel for the State: Ms. Ankita Chaudhary, Dy. AG, Gopal Jha, Ms. Rashmi Singhania, Ms. Himanshi Shakya, Kumar Prashant, Nishant Verma, Shreyash Bhardwaj
investigation_status: Charges framed, final report filed on 27.06.2017, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and death sentence; High Court: Upheld conviction and sentence; Supreme Court: Partly allowed, converted death sentence to life imprisonment for 30 years without remission
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the Appellant and 'S' were present at the function at the house of 'AM', and the medical evidence showed that the deceased was raped and killed. The DNA profiling of the articles found on the deceased matched the blood samples of 'S' and the Appellant, and the Appellant failed to prove an alibi. The prosecution also emphasized the gravity of the crime and the need for a severe punishment.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the Appellant was not given a fair opportunity to defend himself, as the trial and sentencing were rushed. They contended that the chain of circumstances was incomplete and not consistent with a single hypothesis proving the Appellant's guilt. They also argued that the death sentence violated the right to fair trial under Article 21 of the Constitution and that mitigating circumstances were not considered.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that death sentence cannot be imposed except in the rarest of rare cases, and that the probability of reformation and rehabilitation of the accused must be considered. The Court emphasized the need for a bifurcated hearing for conviction and sentencing to ensure a fair trial.
precedent_relied_upon: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 684; Rajendra Pralhadrao Wasnik v. State of Maharashtra (2019) 12 SCC 460; Mofil Khan and Another v. The State of Jharkhand RP (Crl.) No.641 of 2015 in Crl. A. 1795 of 2009; Santosh Kumar Satishbhushan Bariyar v. State of Maharashtra (2009) 6 SCC 498
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed considering the barbaric and savage manner in which the offences of rape and murder were committed on an 11-year-old girl, but the death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment for 30 years without remission due to the Appellant's lack of criminal antecedents, belonging to a Scheduled Tribes community, and the probability of his rehabilitation.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The Appellant was aged 25, belonged to a Scheduled Tribes community, and was eking his livelihood by doing manual labour. He had no criminal antecedents and there was nothing adverse reported against his conduct in jail.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The Appellant committed the heinous crimes of kidnapping, rape, and murder of an 11-year-old girl in a barbaric and savage manner.
other_sentence_order: The conviction under Sections 363, 366A, 364, 346, 376D, 376A, 302, 201 of IPC and Section 5(g)(m) read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act was upheld, and the sentence was converted from death to life imprisonment for 30 years without remission.
